subject: Private Host Integrations — deployment evidence & operator access mapping
messages:
From: Sara Patel <sara@lumenhealth.com>
To: chloe.martin@redwood.ai
Cc: procurement@lumenhealth.com
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Intro: Private host integration questionnaire

Hi Chloe,

Thanks for the quick intro on Monday. We're starting the intake for procurement & security at LumenHealth and need a concise evidence pack that maps operator access, network boundaries, and KMS key flows for your private deployment option (VPC / air-gapped). Our security team provided a short questionnaire (see bullet list below) — can you confirm whether Redwood can provide the items and, if so, send any artifacts or references?

Questions (short):
- Operator roles and separation: who can execute operator-level commands; can operators be scoped to a single customer?
- KMS / HSM: supported key management flows for private and on-prem (bring-your-own-key details).
- Network egress controls & whitelisting approach for updates/telemetry.
- Evidence: any runbooks, network diagrams, or SOC2/attestation references we can attach to our record.

Timeline: procurement hopes to close the security pass within two weeks. Can you confirm feasibility and an initial delivery by EOD Friday?

Regards,

Sara Patel
Senior Security Program Manager
LumenHealth

--
Attachment: Lumen_Security_Questionnaire_v1.pdf (form)

From: chloe.martin@redwood.ai <chloe.martin@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Patel <sara@lumenhealth.com>
Cc: vanessa.ortiz@redwood.ai, jordan.blake@redwood.ai
Date: Wed, 11 Mar 2026 11:23:00 -0700
Subject: RE: Intro: Private host integration questionnaire

Hi Sara — thanks for the note and the questionnaire. We're aligned to support LumenHealth's procurement timeline. I put together an initial evidence workbook and a network diagram that answers each of the bullets; attaching both. Highlights below so your security team can triage quickly: 

- Operator roles and separation: Redwood supports customer-scoped operator accounts in Private deployments. Operators can be limited to a single customer tenant via RBAC bindings in the private control plane; for air-gapped installs customers can optionally provision a jump-host with operator MFA and bastioning.
- KMS / HSM: We support customer-managed KMS (BYOK) via AWS KMS, Azure KeyVault, and on-prem HSM integrations. Keys for disk and token encryption are never exported by Redwood; we store only key references and perform server-side unwrap/rotate operations per customer policy.
- Network egress & updates: For air-gapped installs we provide an accepted update bundle which can be pushed via an offline media workflow; telemetry is configurable (on/off) and when enabled is sent over customer-controlled egress to whitelisted endpoints.

Attachments included: redwood-private-evidence-v1.xlsx (answers + artifacts index), network-segmentation-diagram.pdf (high level). There's an excerpt of the operator runbook in the workbook; full runbook is sensitive but can be shared under NDA/secure link.

Deliverable ETA: I can deliver the workbook and diagram today and follow up with a short operator-access matrix by Friday. If procurement wants a signed attestation (SOC2 reference + statement of controls) we can include a SOC2 summary and the relevant page numbers.

Next steps: Let me know if you want a 30-minute call tomorrow to walk security through the workbook.

Best,

Chloe Martin
Senior Solutions Architect, Deployments

Chloe — adding a couple clarifications from the product side before we hand artifacts to Lumen:

1) Operator scoping: for Dedicated and Private we offer two operator models — (A) shared platform operators (Redwood-managed) with strict scoping via namespaces and (B) customer-operator model where the customer runs operator accounts in their environment and we provide automation bundles. Please ensure the worksheet clarifies both models and the recommended default for healthcare customers.

2) KMS proofs: procurement will want a concise sequence diagram for the BYOK flow (key wrapping/unwrapping). Can you add an appendix with the sequence (client -> KMS -> Redwood runtime) and identify where plaintext keys are handled (none in our controls).

3) Evidence gating: full runbooks require an evidence sharing agreement. We should offer a temporary secure share link (S3 presigned or internal secure portal) instead of listing runbook text inline.

I'll review the workbook now; I flagged two rows where we should tighten language on telemetry retention.

-Vanessa
Director, Product Operations

- Please include the BYOK sequence diagram appendix (Vanessa's suggestion) and call out any operator-facing endpoints that accept secrets.
- Telemetry: provisioning must include a retention cap and an option to disable telemetry entirely for our airs-gapped workload. Please mark the workbook cell with an explicit default and the 'disable' option.
- Evidence sharing: procurement can accept a secure, time-limited link to the runbook and signed attestation PDFs. Can you provide a presigned link or DocuSign reference for the SOC2 extract?

Procurement timeline: we'll aim to finish the intake and vendor review by next Thursday. Once security signs off, procurement will circulate a standard SOW and a single redline round.

For context I'm copying our infrastructure lead Tom in case he wants to join a call about network boundaries.

Sara

Sara — appreciate the checklist. Quick confirmations and next steps: 

- BYOK appendix: attached an additional sheet in redwood-private-evidence-v1.xlsx titled "BYOK_sequence_appendix" that diagrams the wrap/unwrap flow; no plaintext keys are ever persisted by Redwood.
- Operator-facing secret endpoints: the only operator endpoint that accepts wrapped secrets is the operator API within the private control plane; unwrapped secrets are only present transiently in memory during the bootstrap process and under customer-controlled KMS. We've annotated the workbook row (sheet: Controls) and added a short note in the runbook excerpt.
- Telemetry: default retention is 30 days; the workbook lists configurable options (0 / 7 / 30 / custom) and explicitly documents the "disable telemetry" path for air-gapped installs.
- Evidence share: I prepared a presigned S3 link for the runbook excerpt and the SOC2 extract (valid 7 days). Sending the secure share via our portal — link below. If procurement needs a DocuSign acknowledgement, we can route the SOC2 summary through DocuSign as well.
